A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SP-Mind research and provide readable text, figures, tables, algorithms, and equations. Appendices A–E are identical apart from page numbers, supporting a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent evaluations on SP-Bench, CRC-CODEX quantification, and cell annotation in Tables 1–3, together with qualitative execution analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendices A–B retain the same skill retrieval, prompt assembly, ReAct/CodeAct execution, tool library, and session management. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 102 SP-Bench queries, 10 CRC-CODEX images, and four cell-annotation datasets. SpatialBench is newly discussed as related work but is not evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in each of Tables 1–3, including the generalist agents, Biomni-SP, ToolUniverse-SP, the no-skill variant, and ASTIR where applicable. The same exclusions are documented.

E3.justification: The Claude Sonnet 4 backbone, sample sizes, difficulty tiers, evaluation metrics, and testing procedures are retained. Appendices C–E preserve the 30-minute timeout, data preparation, annotation scoring, and quantification protocols.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same no-skill ablations, stitching and cell-annotation case studies, and file-management/background-subtraction failure analysis. No robustness or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same three-run reporting and mean/standard-deviation practice. Appendix E also retains the MMD estimator, subsampling procedure, and fixed random seed of 42.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–3 match, including SP-Mind's 68.9% SP-Bench average, 0.953 quantification Pearson correlation, and 0.681 average annotation score. The figures and qualitative findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations (1)–(7) in Appendices D–E are unchanged. No assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations are introduced or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about autonomous spatial-proteomics analysis, SP-Bench's novelty, and performance against existing agents. The added code-availability statement does not revise these scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of performance and failures remain unchanged, including uneven skill transfer to PDAC IMC, workflow bookkeeping problems, and dependence on human-curated templates. The new SpatialBench discussion concerns research positioning.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit public-code statement and GitHub repository link in the abstract, absent from v1. Implementation and evaluation documentation otherwise matches; the PDFs alone do not establish the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens literature coverage through new references on multimodal LLMs, biomedical models, scientific reasoning, RL, and clinical safety. It also newly distinguishes SP-Bench from SpatialBench by contrasting spatial transcriptomics with pixel-intensive multiplexed-immunofluorescence proteomics.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the expanded Biomedical AI Agents and Agent Benchmarks paragraphs, the abstract's code statement, and small wording corrections. The section hierarchy and the remaining scientific narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 move together from page 7 to page 8, with surrounding text reflowing. Their formatting and captions remain unchanged, as do all figure images; the appendices retain their layouts apart from page numbers.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a concrete code-access pointer and acknowledges SpatialBench with an explicit explanation of the intended benchmark distinction. These improve access information and contextualization, but the methods, empirical support, and limitations are unchanged. The broader citation additions do not establish stronger validation, and repository quality cannot be assessed from the PDFs.
